fields.title: The Model as an External Dependency
fields.keyTakeaway: An AI provider is an external dependency with four failure modes, including a refusal to answer, and a plan B for each feature is designed in advance.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: The model provider is down for 20 minutes. What does the user see?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: An AI provider is just as much of an [[external-dependency|external dependency]] as a payment gateway, and obeys the rules from `IN1-N5`. The difference is that people often think of it as part of the product rather than someone else's system — and fail to design a plan B.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: Four ways an AI provider fails, and they differ from regular ones:
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/text: *Outage.* Regular failure. *Slowdown.* More dangerous: generation is already slow, doubling it exceeds user patience. *Rate limiting.* Providers limit tokens per minute. During a spike, it hits limits faster than expected. *Refusal to answer.* The model is available and refuses. Technically a success, product-wise a failure.
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: **Another model.** [[model-cascade|Cascade]] or another provider. Requires the prompt to work on both — verified by evals beforehand. **Cached response.** For recurring queries. **Non-generative replacement.** Show data without the model: ingredients as is, list of products without recommendation. **Honest refusal.** With explanation and timeframe.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: The fourth level is more acceptable for AI features than for payments: the feature is usually auxiliary. But the decision must be made, not left to chance.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: Separately — **rate limits as a product constraint.** The provider gives N tokens per minute. During a spike, the feature stops working for some people. Exactly who gets refused is a product decision: priority to paying users, priority to started sessions, a fair queue.
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/rows/0/1: Show description and ingredients as is, without an answer
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: The second option turned out valuable on its own: "repeat past order" was used by 14% even when the assistant was working.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: Limits: when exhausted, priority goes to users with an active recommendation session — interrupting mid-session is worse than not starting. New users see "assistant is busy, try again in a minute".
fields.sections/3/blocks/4/text: Slowdown: 12-second timeout on generation, if exceeded — plan B. Introduced after an incident where the provider took 40 seconds to respond and people waited because streaming created the illusion of work.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: Switching between providers requires prompts and formats to be compatible. This limits the use of specific features of a single provider.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: An AI provider is an external dependency with four failure modes, including a refusal to answer, and a plan B for each feature is designed in advance.
